newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Novorossiisk halts oil shipments for 86 hours.
newsitem.headline: Novorossiisk halts oil shipments for 86 hours.

text.p: Russia's main Black Sea oil export outlet of Novorossiisk stopped shipping crude oil from 9 a.m. local time on Tuesday for 86 hours due to pipeline repairs and empty storage tanks, a dispatcher on duty told Reuters.
"The pipeline is closed and there is no oil in the cisterns to ship," the dispatcher said.
The closure took place at 0600 GMT.
Interfax news agency said three vessels of 75,000 tonnes, 80,000 tonnes and 125,000 tonnes had been waiting to load.
"They will have to wait until the pipeline starts working again," the dispatcher said, adding that the Chernomorsk region, not the port, was handling the repairs.

Novorossiisk's crude oil storage tank capacity is estimated at between 500,000 tonnes (3.65 million barrels) and 700,000 tonnes (5.10 million barrels). The dispatcher did not specify how long the tanks had been empty.
Interfax said that a vessel that had loaded 135,000 tonnes of oil before the closure was scheduled to leave the port, but gave no further details.
The dispatcher could not say which section of the trunk oil pipeline feeding the outlet was being repaired or why.

The largest crude oil loading berth in Novorossiisk may close for up to 16 days in December for maintenance, but port officials said last week the repairs' schedule had not yet been approved in detail.
